<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"><B>WHY DID I RECEIVE A NOTICE IN THE MAIL REGARDING THE INTERNET AVAILABILITY OF PROXY MATERIALS INSTEAD OF A FULL SET OF PROXY MATERIALS?</B></TD></TR>

<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;" ALIGN="right">A:</TD>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"><B>WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN HOLDING SHARES AS A STOCKHOLDER OF RECORD AND AS A BENEFICIAL OWNER?</B></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">
<TD HEIGHT="4"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="4" COLSPAN="4"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="4" COLSPAN="2"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:3pt">&nbsp;</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;" ALIGN="right">A:</TD>
<TD NOWRAP VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Most of our stockholders hold their shares as a beneficial owner through a broker or other nominee rather than directly
in their own name. As summarized below, there are some distinctions between shares held of record and those owned beneficially.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Stockholder of Record</U>. If your shares are registered directly in your name with our transfer agent, Computershare Trust Company, N.A., you are considered, with
respect to those shares, the&nbsp;stockholder of record,&nbsp;and the Notice was sent directly to you. As the&nbsp;stockholder of record,&nbsp;you have the right to grant your voting proxy directly to AMD or to vote at our Annual Meeting. If you
requested to receive printed proxy materials, we have enclosed a proxy card for you to use, as described in the Notice and under Question 10 below. You may also vote on the Internet, or by telephone, as described in the Notice and under Question 10
below. You are also invited to attend our Annual Meeting via the Internet.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Beneficial
Owner</U>. If your shares are held in an account in the name of a brokerage firm, bank, broker-dealer, trust or other similar organization (i.e., in street name), like the vast majority of our stockholders, you are considered the beneficial owner of
shares held in street name, and the Notice should be forwarded to you by that organization. As the beneficial owner, you have the right to direct your broker or other nominee how to vote your shares, and you are also invited to attend our Annual

<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As a beneficial owner, in order to ensure your shares are voted, you must provide voting instructions to your broker or
other nominee by the deadline provided in the materials you receive from your broker or other nominee. If you do not provide voting instructions to your broker or other nominee, whether your shares can be voted by such person depends on the type of
item being considered for vote.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Discretionary</FONT>
Items</U>. The election of directors and the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Say-on-Pay</FONT></FONT> proposal are <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-discretionary</FONT> items and may not be voted on by brokers
or other nominees who have not received specific voting instructions from beneficial owners. A broker <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-vote</FONT> occurs when your broker or other nominee has not received instructions from you as to how to vote
your shares on a proposal and does not have discretionary authority to vote your shares on that proposal.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Discretionary Items</U>. The ratification of the appointment of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as our independent registered public accounting firm for the current fiscal
year is a discretionary item. Generally, brokers and other nominees that do not receive voting instructions from beneficial owners may vote on these proposals in their discretion.</P></TD></TR>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"><B>WHAT IS A &#147;QUORUM&#148;?</B></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">
<TD HEIGHT="4"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="4" COLSPAN="4"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="4" COLSPAN="2"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:3pt">&nbsp;</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;" ALIGN="right">A:</TD>
<TD NOWRAP VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;">For the purposes of our Annual Meeting, a &#147;quorum&#148; is the presence, in person or by proxy, by the holders of a majority of the voting power of the outstanding shares entitled to vote at our
Annual Meeting. There must be a quorum for our Annual Meeting to be held. Both abstentions and broker <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-votes</FONT> are counted for the purpose of determining the presence of a quorum.</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt" BGCOLOR="#d8d8d8">
<TD HEIGHT="5"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="5" COLSPAN="4"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="5" COLSPAN="2"></TD></TR>
<TR BGCOLOR="#d8d8d8" STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;">&nbsp;17.</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"><B>&nbsp;</B></TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;" ALIGN="right"><B>Q:</B></TD>
<TD NOWRAP VALIGN="top" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"><B>&nbsp;</B></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;"><B>WHAT IS THE VOTING REQUIREMENT FOR EACH PROPOSAL TO PASS?</B></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">
<TD HEIGHT="4"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="4" COLSPAN="4"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="4" COLSPAN="2"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:3pt">&nbsp;</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" ALIGN="right">A:</TD>
<TD NOWRAP VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Election of Directors</U>. Each of the eight director nominees will be elected if each of them receives the affirmative vote of a majority of the
votes cast. A majority of the votes cast means that the number of votes cast &#147;for&#148; a director must exceed the number of votes cast &#147;against&#148; that director. Abstentions and broker <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-votes</FONT>
will have no effect on the outcome of these elections. Each director nominee has submitted a written resignation that will be effective if he or she does not receive a majority of the votes cast for such director and the resignation is accepted by
the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, another authorized committee of the Board or the Board.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Ratification of the Appointment of our Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</U>. Ratification of the appointment of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as our
independent registered public accounting firm requires the affirmative vote of a majority of the shares of our common stock entitled to vote and present in person or represented by proxy at the Annual Meeting. Abstentions have the same effect as a
vote against this proposal. Because brokers and other nominees have discretionary authority to vote on the ratification, we do not expect any broker <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-votes</FONT> in connection with this item.</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Say-On-Pay</FONT></FONT>
Proposal</U>.&nbsp;Approval, on an advisory basis, of the compensation of our named executive officers as disclosed in this proxy statement pursuant to the compensation disclosure rules of the SEC, requires the affirmative vote of a majority of the
shares of our common stock entitled to vote and present in person or represented by proxy at the Annual Meeting. Because your vote is advisory, it will not be binding on the Board, the Compensation and Leadership Resources Committee (the
&#147;Compensation Committee&#148;) or us.</P></TD></TR></TABLE>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_3"></A>ITEM&nbsp;1&#151;ELECTION OF DIRECTORS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our Board currently consists of eight members. On the recommendation of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, the Board has nominated the
following eight nominees: Mr.&nbsp;John&nbsp;E.&nbsp;Caldwell, Ms.&nbsp;Nora&nbsp;M.&nbsp;Denzel, Mr.&nbsp;Mark Durcan, Mr.&nbsp;Michael&nbsp;P. Gregoire, Mr.&nbsp;Joseph&nbsp;A. Householder, Mr.&nbsp;John&nbsp;W.&nbsp;Marren,
Dr.&nbsp;Lisa&nbsp;T.&nbsp;Su and Mr.&nbsp;Abhi&nbsp;Y. Talwalkar for election to the Board at the Annual Meeting. All directors are elected annually and serve a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> term until our next annual meeting or
until such director&#146;s successor is appointed. Proxies cannot be voted for a greater number of persons than the number of nominees named in this proxy statement. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board expects all nominees named below to be available for election. If a nominee declines or is unable to act as a director, your proxy may vote for
any substitute nominee proposed by the Board. Your proxy will vote <B>FOR</B> the election of these nominees, unless you instruct otherwise. Directors are strongly encouraged to attend annual meetings of our stockholders. At the 2020 Annual Meeting
of Stockholders, the directors in attendance were: Mr.&nbsp;Caldwell, Ms.&nbsp;Denzel, Mr.&nbsp;Durcan, Mr.&nbsp;Gregoire, Mr.&nbsp;Householder, Mr.&nbsp;Marren, Dr.&nbsp;Su and Mr.&nbsp;Talwalkar. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_4"></A>Director Experience, Skills and Qualifications </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our goal is to assemble a knowledgeable and highly-qualified Board that operates cohesively and works with management in a constructive way to deliver
long-term value to our stockholders. We believe that the nominees set forth below, all of whom are currently directors of AMD, possess valuable experience necessary to guide us in the best interests of our stockholders. Our current Board consists of
individuals with proven records of success in their chosen professions. They possess the highest integrity and a keen intellect.&nbsp;They are collegial, yet independent in their thinking, and are committed to the hard work necessary to be informed
about the semiconductor industry, us and our key constituents, including our customers, stockholders and management. Most of our directors have broad technology sector experience, including expertise in semiconductor technology, innovation and
strategy. Several members of the Board are current or former chief executive officers, thereby providing the Board with practical understanding of how large organizations operate, including the importance of employee development and retention. They
also understand strategy and risk management and how these factors impact our operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Certain information regarding each of the nominees is set
forth below, including his or her experience, qualifications, attributes and skills that led the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and the Board to conclude that the individual should serve as a director on the Board, as well as his or
her principal occupation. Each nominee&#146;s former directorships on public company boards during the past five years are included in a table set forth below&#151;Former Directorships During the Last Five Years. The age of each director is as of
our Annual Meeting. </P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_5"></A>Consideration of Stockholder Nominees for Director </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The policy of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee is to consider properly submitted stockholder nominations for candidates to serve on the
Board. Pursuant to our bylaws, stockholders who wish to nominate persons for election to the Board at our 2022 annual meeting of stockholders must be a stockholder of record, both when they give us notice and at our 2022 annual meeting, must be
entitled to vote at our 2022 annual meeting and must comply with the notice provisions in our bylaws. A stockholder&#146;s notice must be delivered to our Corporate Secretary not less than 90&nbsp;days nor more than 120 days before the anniversary
date of the immediately preceding annual meeting. For our 2022 annual meeting of stockholders, the notice must be delivered between January&nbsp;19, 2022 and February&nbsp;18, 2022. However, if our 2022 annual meeting of stockholders is not held
within 30 days of May&nbsp;19, 2022, the stockholder&#146;s notice must be delivered no later than the close of business on the tenth day following the earlier of the day on which the first public announcement of the date of our 2022 annual meeting
was </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Anyone who wishes to communicate with our Board or with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> directors may send their communications in
writing to Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., 2485 Augustine Drive, Santa Clara, California 95054, Attention: Corporate Secretary or send an email to <U>Corporate.Secretary@amd.com</U>. Our Corporate Secretary will forward all of these communications to
our Chairman of the Board. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_7"></A>Required Vote </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">At our Annual Meeting, our directors will be elected using a majority vote standard with respect to uncontested elections, such as this election. This
standard requires that each director receive the affirmative vote of a majority of the votes cast. A majority of the votes cast means that the number of votes cast &#147;for&#148; a director must exceed the number of votes cast &#147;against&#148;
that director. Abstentions and broker <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-votes</FONT> will have no effect on the outcome of these director elections. Each director nominee has submitted a written resignation that will be effective if he or she
does not receive a majority of the votes cast for such director and the resignation is accepted by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, another authorized Board committee or the Board. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_8"></A>Recommendation of the Board Directors </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B>The Board of Directors unanimously recommends that you vote FOR each of the director nominees. Unless you vote otherwise, your proxy will vote FOR the
proposed nominees. </B></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_9"></A>CORPORATE GOVERNANCE </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board has adopted the Governance Principles to address significant corporate governance matters. The Governance Principles provide a framework for
our corporate governance matters and include topics such as Board and Board committee composition and evaluation. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee is responsible for reviewing the Governance Principles and recommending any changes
to the Governance Principles to the Board. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_10"></A>Independence of Directors </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Governance Principles provide that a substantial majority of the members of the Board must meet the criteria for independence as required by
applicable law and the listing rules of the Nasdaq Stock Market (&#147;Nasdaq&#148;). Among other criteria, no director qualifies as independent unless the Board determines that the director has no direct material relationship which, in the opinion
of the Board, would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the responsibilities of a director. On an annual basis, the Board undertakes a review of director independence. The Board determined that all directors who
served during fiscal 2020 and all of our director nominees, other than Dr.&nbsp;Su, are independent in accordance with SEC and Nasdaq rules. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In
making its independence determinations, the Board reviewed direct and indirect transactions and relationships between each director, or any member of his or her immediate family, and us or one of our subsidiaries or affiliates based on information
provided by the director, our records and publicly available information. All of the reviewed transactions and arrangements were entered into in the ordinary course of business and none of the transactions or arrangements involved an amount that
(i)&nbsp;exceeded the greater of 5% of the recipient entity&#146;s revenues or $200,000 with respect to transactions where a director or any member of his or her immediate family or spouse served in any capacity other than as a director
of&nbsp;a&nbsp;publicly held corporation or (ii)&nbsp;exceeded $10,000 with&nbsp;respect to professional or consulting services provided by entities at which our directors serve as professors or employees. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board determined that none of our directors currently has or has had any direct or indirect material interest in any transactions and arrangements
that would interfere with their exercise of independent judgment as members of the Board. The Board also determined that each of the members of the Audit and Finance, Nominating and Corporate Governance and Compensation and Leadership Resources<I>
</I>Committees are independent in accordance with SEC and Nasdaq rules. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_11"></A>Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">During fiscal 2020, Ms.&nbsp;Denzel and Messrs. Durcan and Talwalkar served on the Compensation and Leadership Resources Committee (the
&#147;Compensation Committee&#148;). None of the members of the Compensation Committee is or has been an executive officer or employee of AMD. In addition, none of our executive officers serves on the board of directors or compensation committee of
a company which has an executive officer who serves on our Board or Compensation Committee. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_12"></A>Board Leadership Structure </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Governance Principles permit the roles of Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer to be filled by the same or different individuals, based
on our needs, best practices and the interests of our stockholders. This allows the Board flexibility to determine whether the two roles should be combined or separated based upon our needs and the Board&#146;s assessment of its leadership from time
to time.&nbsp;The Board has the experience of functioning effectively either way. The Board believes that its current leadership structure, with an independent Chairman of the Board, separate from the Chief Executive Officer, is the most appropriate
leadership structure for the Company at this time, is in the best interests of the stockholders and allows the Board to fulfill its duties effectively and efficiently based on our current needs. Mr.&nbsp;Caldwell, who is independent in accordance
with SEC and Nasdaq rules, is our Chairman of the Board. Mr.&nbsp;Caldwell presides at meetings of our stockholders and directors and leads the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities. The Board benefits from Mr.&nbsp;Caldwell&#146;s extensive and
diversified leadership experience, financial management and risk assessment experience. He also has strong public company board experience and has intimate familiarity with our history and business. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Separating the roles of the Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer also enables the independent directors to more meaningfully participate in
the leadership of the Board. The Board currently believes this structure provides an appropriate degree of oversight and allows Dr.&nbsp;Su, our President and Chief Executive Officer, to focus on our business strategy and market opportunities, as
well as on our organizational structure and execution capabilities. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_13"></A>Risk Oversight </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board&#146;s role in risk oversight is consistent with our leadership structure, with our Chief Executive Officer and other members of management
having responsibility for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> risk management activities and processes, and our Board and its committees being actively involved in overseeing our risk
management. The Board and management consider &#147;risk&#148; for these purposes to be the possibility of an undesired occurrence that could threaten the viability of the company, result in a material destruction of our assets or stockholder value,
or materially impact our long-term performance. Examples of the types of risks faced by us include: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">business-specific risks related to our ability to develop new products and services, our strategic position in key existing
and new markets, our operational execution and infrastructure, our relationships with our third-party manufacturing suppliers and competition in the microprocessor and graphics markets; </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">macroeconomic risks, such as adverse global economic conditions and global
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">geo-political</FONT> events; and </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">&#147;event&#148; risks, such as pandemics, natural disasters and cybersecurity threats. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">During 2020, the Board and its committees also discussed with management strategies to address the impact of
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</FONT> on employees and our business operations and practices, including taking measures to protect the health and safety of our employees and monitoring demand signals to assess supply chain requirements
and product schedules and roadmaps. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We engage in value-creating strategies and activities that appropriately balances returns with risk. We mitigate
potential exposures through our proactive risk management systems. Our senior management participates in the identification and assessment of the inherent risks that impact our business and develops processes and controls and other measures designed
to mitigate those risks. Our Chief Executive Officer has ultimate responsibility for management of our business, including enterprise level risks and the risk management program and processes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In fulfilling its oversight role, the Board focuses on understanding the nature of our enterprise risks, including risks in our operations, finance and
strategy, organization, compliance and external exposures as well as the adequacy of our risk assessment and risk management processes. The Board has implemented a risk oversight model that delegates certain risks to its committees and retains other
risks at the Board-level. The Board and committees periodically receive reports and updates from management. At least annually, the Board discusses with management the appropriate level of risk relative to our strategy and objectives and reviews
with management our existing risk management processes and their effectiveness. The Board also receives periodic management updates on our operations, organization, financial position and results and strategy and, as appropriate, discusses and
provides feedback with respect to risks related to these topics. In addition, the Board receives full reports from the following Board committee chairs regarding each committee&#146;s considerations and actions related to the specific risk topics
over which the committee has oversight: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

company&#146;s financial and information technology (including product security and cybersecurity) risk exposures; reviews our portfolio of risk; discusses with management significant financial, reporting, regulatory and legal compliance risks in
conjunction with enterprise risk exposures as well as risks associated with our capital structure; reviews our policies with respect to risk assessment and risk management and the actions management has taken to limit, monitor or control financial
and enterprise risk exposure; business continuity; and emerging risks. The Audit and Finance Committee meets with members of our Internal Audit department to discuss any issues that warrant attention. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

talent management and development applicable to all employees . It reviews with management whether our compensation programs may create incentives for our employees to take excessive or inappropriate risks which could be reasonably likely to have a
material adverse effect on us. For additional details, see &#147;Compensation Policies and Practices,&#148; below. Additionally, the Compensation Committee oversees organizational risks, including leadership succession, talent capacity,
capabilities, attraction, retention and culture. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_14"></A>Code of Ethics </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board has adopted a code of ethics that applies to all directors and employees entitled the &#147;Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct,&#148;
which is designed to help directors and employees resolve ethical issues encountered in the business environment. The Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct covers topics such as conflicts of interest, compliance with laws (including
anti-corruption laws), fair dealing, protecting our property and confidentiality of our information and encourages the reporting of any behavior not in accordance with the Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board has also adopted a &#147;Code of Ethics&#148; for our executive officers and all other senior finance executives. The Code of Ethics covers
topics such as financial reporting, conflicts of interest and compliance with laws, rules, regulations and our policies. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_16"></A>Board Meetings and Attendance </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The
Board held 15 meetings during 2020 and all members of the Board attended at least&nbsp;75&nbsp;percent of the meetings of the Board and Board committees on which they served. In addition, on at least an annual basis, the Board and management discuss
our strategic direction, new business opportunities and product roadmap. Independent and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> directors also meet regularly in scheduled executive sessions without our Chief Executive Officer and
other members of senior management. In addition to these formal meetings, members of our Board informally interact with senior management (including our Chief Executive Officer), industry leaders and customers on a periodic basis. In 2020, sessions
of only our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors were held five times. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_17"></A>Board Committees </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board has four standing committees: an Audit and Finance Committee, a Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, a Compensation and Leadership
Resources Committee and an Innovation and Technology Committee. The members of the Board committees and their Chairs are nominated by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and appointed by the Board. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Each of the Board committees has adopted a written charter, which has been approved by the Board. You can access our current bylaws, committee charters,
the Governance Principles, the Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct and the Code of Ethics on the Investor Relations pages of our website at <U>www.amd.com</U> or <U>ir.amd.com</U>. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Audit and Finance Committee.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Audit and Finance Committee assists the Board with its oversight responsibilities
regarding the integrity of our financial statements, our compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, risk assessment, the performance of our internal audit function, our financial affairs and policies and the nature and structure of major
financial commitments. The Audit and Finance Committee is also directly responsible for the appointment, independence, compensation, retention and oversight of the work of our independent registered public accounting firm, which reports directly to
the Audit and Finance Committee. The Audit and Finance Committee meets alone with our senior management, our financial, legal and internal audit personnel and with our independent registered public accounting firm, which has free access to the Audit
and Finance Committee. The head of our Internal Audit Department reports directly to the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee and &#147;dotted-line&#148; to our Chief Financial Officer and serves a staff function for the Audit and Finance
Committee. The Audit and Finance Committee currently consists of Mr.&nbsp;Householder, as Chair, and Messrs.&nbsp;Caldwell, Gregoire and Marren, each determined to be financially literate and &#147;independent&#148; under applicable SEC and Nasdaq
rules. The Board also determined that Mr.&nbsp;Householder is an &#147;audit committee financial expert,&#148; as defined under applicable SEC rules. The Audit and Finance Committee held nine meetings during 2020. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Nominating and
Corporate Governance Committee assists the Board in its responsibilities regarding the identification of qualified candidates to become Board members, the selection of nominees for election as directors at the next annual meeting of stockholders (or
special meeting of stockholders at which directors are to be elected), the selection of candidates to fill any vacancies on the Board and the development and recommendation to the Board of corporate governance guidelines and principles, including
the Governance Principles, as well as matters related to environmental and social issues (ESG), practices and reporting. In addition, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee oversees the Board&#146;s annual review of its performance
(including its composition and organization) and leads a process for our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors to evaluate the performance of our Chief Executive Officer. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee
retains a search firm for the purpose of obtaining information regarding potential candidates for Board membership. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee currently consists of Mr.&nbsp;Caldwell, as Chair, Ms.&nbsp;Denzel and Messrs.
Durcan, Gregoire, Householder, Marren and Talwalkar, each determined by the Board to be &#147;independent&#148; under applicable SEC and Nasdaq rules. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee held four meetings during 2020. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In evaluating candidates to determine if they are qualified to become Board members, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee looks principally
for the following attributes: personal and professional character, integrity, ethics and values; diversity and inclusion; general business experience and leadership profile, including experience in corporate management, such as serving as an officer
or former officer of a publicly held company; strategic planning abilities and experience; aptitude in accounting and finance; expertise in domestic and international markets; experience in our industry and with relevant social policy concerns;
understanding of relevant technologies; expertise in an area of our operations; communication and interpersonal skills; and practical and mature business judgment. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee also considers Board members&#146;
and nominees&#146; service on the boards of other public companies. In an effort to foster and maintain a diversity of viewpoints on the Board, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee will monitor the mix of skills and experience of Board
members and assess potential candidates in the context of the current make-up of the Board and the needs of the Company. Further, other than when the Company is obligated by contract or otherwise, the initial list of candidates from which new
management-supported Director nominees are chosen shall include qualified female and racially/ethnically diverse candidates. Any third-party consultant asked to furnish such a list of candidates will be instructed to include such candidates. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Compensation and Leadership Resources Committee.</I><I></I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Compensation Committee assists the Board in its
responsibilities relating to the compensation of all Section&nbsp;16 officers, members of the Board and such other employees as delegated from time to time by the Board. In consultation with management, the Board and the Compensation
Committee&#146;s compensation consultant, the Compensation Committee designs, recommends to the Board for approval and evaluates our compensation plans, policies and programs. In addition, the Compensation Committee provides guidance on our talent
management and development programs, including but not limited to those regarding talent acquisition, retention, talent development, succession planning, career progression, culture, diversity and inclusion. With respect to our Section&nbsp;16
officers, the Compensation Committee reviews and approves all grants to the Board, our executive officers, senior vice presidents, and Section&nbsp;16 officers under our equity plans. To the extent permitted by its charter, the Compensation
Committee may delegate certain authority and certain responsibilities to one or more of its members, our officers or a subcommittee of the Compensation Committee. The Compensation Committee aims to structure our compensation program to encourage
high performance, promote accountability and align employee interests with our strategic goals and with the interests of our stockholders. The Compensation Committee also oversees risk management as it relates to our compensation policies and
practices for employees generally. </P>

product development and investment and protection of the company&#146;s intellectual property; reviewing, evaluating and making recommendations regarding talent and skills of our workforce supporting our technology and research and development
activities; monitoring the performance of our technology development in support of our overall business strategy; monitoring and evaluating existing and future trends in technology that may affect our strategic plans, including monitoring overall
industry trends; and assessing our risk mitigation policies and procedures relating to products based on new technology or significant innovations to existing technology. The Innovation and Technology Committee currently consists of Mr.&nbsp;Durcan,
as Chair, Ms.&nbsp;Denzel and Mr.&nbsp;Talwalker. The Innovation and Technology Committee held four meetings during 2020. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_18"></A>DIRECTORS&#146; COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our directors play a critical role in guiding our strategic direction and overseeing our management. In order to compensate them for their substantial
time commitment, we provide a mix of cash and equity-based compensation. While we reimburse our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors for expenses incurred in connection with their service on our Board, we do not provide
perquisites, pension or retirement benefits to our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>2020 <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Director Compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;</I>The table below summarizes the compensation paid to our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors for 2020. Dr.&nbsp;Su, who is an employee
director, did not receive any additional compensation for her service as a director on the Board. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

</TABLE></DIV> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Determining <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Director
Compensation.</I><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;</I>The Compensation Committee annually reviews our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors&#146; compensation. Based on this review, the Compensation Committee recommends any changes to our
non-employee directors&#146; compensation to the Board for approval. In addition, the Board and Compensation Committee periodically evaluate how our director pay levels and pay policies compare to the competitive market. In 2020, the Board and
Compensation Committee reviewed competitive market data regarding <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors&#146; pay relative to our peer group (as described in more detail in the &#147;Compensation Discussion and
Analysis&#148; section) as well as the broader market which was compiled by Compensia, the independent compensation consultant of our Compensation Committee. While competitive market data is important to the evaluation of the directors&#146;
compensation, such data is just one of several factors considered by the Board in approving director compensation, and the Board has discretion in determining the nature and extent of its use. In 2020, in addition to the competitive market data, the
Board considered the amount of time associated with Board and Board committee services as well as annual share usage under our 2004 Equity Incentive Plan (as amended and restated, the &#147;2004 Plan&#148;) related to
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director compensation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Board continued the practice adopted in May 2014, to reallocate the
mix of cash and equity compensation paid to our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors, with the goal of maintaining total average compensation per <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director at
approximately the same level as had been previously paid and maintaining an affordable annual share usage. These changes are further described under &#147;Cash Fees Paid to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Directors&#148; and
&#147;Equity Awards for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Directors,&#148; below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Cash Fees Paid to <FONT

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Equity Awards for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Directors.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;In order to align the
long-term interests of our directors with those of our stockholders, a portion of director compensation is provided in the form of equity. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-employee</FONT> directors participate in the 2004 Plan and are entitled
to receive equity awards under our Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy, subject to the terms of the 2004 Plan. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-employee</FONT> directors are generally eligible to receive an annual RSU award (an
&#147;Annual RSU Award&#148;) upon <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">re-election</FONT> at each annual meeting of stockholders, and, if a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director is appointed to the Board on a date other than the
date of an annual meeting of stockholders, such director is entitled to receive an initial RSU award on his or her appointment to the Board (an <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#147;Off-Cycle</FONT> RSU Grant&#148;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Annual RSU Awards</U>.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under our current Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy, which was amended in February 2020, the Annual RSU
Award for each <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director (other than the Chairman of the Board) who has served on the Board continuously prior to an annual meeting of stockholders is calculated based on the following formula,
with no discretionary component: the quotient of (i)&nbsp;$205,000 (the &#147;Target Equity Value&#148;) divided by (ii)&nbsp;the average closing price of our common stock for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">30-trading</FONT> day period
preceding and ending with the date of the respective RSU grant. The Chairman of the Board&#146;s Annual RSU Award is 1.5x the Target Equity Value. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In addition, under our current Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy, if a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director has served
on the Board for less than twelve months prior to an annual meeting of stockholders, such director&#146;s Annual RSU Award is <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pro-rated</FONT> based on the number of months of service before the respective annual
meeting of stockholders. For purposes of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pro-rata</FONT> calculation, service during any portion of a month counts as a full month of service. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Off-Cycle</FONT> Grants</U>.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under our current Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy, an <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Off-Cycle</FONT> Grant is equal to the quotient of (i)&nbsp;the Target Equity Value divided by (ii)&nbsp;the average closing price of our common stock for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">30-trading</FONT> day period
preceding and ending with the date of the respective RSU grant. The Annual RSU Awards and the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Off-Cycle</FONT> RSU Grants vest on the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> anniversary of their grant dates.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In 2020, each of our directors received an Annual RSU Award under our current Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Deferral</U>.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to our Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy, our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT>
directors may elect to defer the issuance of shares of our common stock that become issuable upon vesting of the RSUs granted pursuant to the 2004 Plan (and the recognition of taxable income associated with such RSUs) until such time as the director
ceases to serve on our Board. A <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director can make this election by completing a Restricted Stock Unit Award Deferral Election Agreement before the scheduled date of an RSU grant.&nbsp;If a
director makes this election, the issuance of the common stock subject to the RSUs may not be accelerated or changed once the Election Agreement is submitted to us.&nbsp;Any common stock deferred under our Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy
is issued to the director, in one lump sum, within 30 days after his or her resignation from our Board. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><U>Acceleration of Vesting</U>.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to our Outside Director Equity Compensation Policy,
in the event of our change of control, all of our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors&#146; equity compensation awards will become fully vested. In addition, in the event of the termination of a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director&#146;s service to the Board as a result of death, disability or retirement, all of his or her equity compensation awards will become fully vested; provided that, such <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director served as a member of the Board for at least three years prior to the date of termination and satisfied our stock ownership guideline requirements during his or her service as a Board member.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Other Benefits for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Directors.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;We reimburse our directors for their travel and
expenses in connection with attending Board meetings and Board-related activities, such as AMD site visits and sponsored events, as well as for continuing education programs. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Stock Ownership Guidelines.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;Under our stock ownership guidelines, which were updated in August 2020, our
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors are required to hold the lesser of (i)&nbsp;the number of shares equivalent to five times their then-current annual retainer divided by the average closing price of our common stock for
the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">30-day</FONT> period immediately preceding and ending with the date of the annual meeting of stockholders or (ii)&nbsp;30,000 shares (in the case of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors
other than the Chairman of our Board) or 45,000 shares (in the case of the Chairman of the Board). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The stock ownership guidelines must be achieved
by each <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director within the later of (i)&nbsp;August 2022 or (ii)&nbsp;the five-year anniversary of the respective director&#146;s first election or appointment to the Board or first appointment
as Chairman of the Board, as applicable. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Until the requirements of our stock ownership guidelines are achieved, each
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director is encouraged to retain at least 10% of the &#147;net shares&#148; (as defined below) obtained through our stock incentive plans. Shares counted toward the minimum stock ownership
requirements include (i)&nbsp;shares of common stock owned outright by a director and his or her immediate family members who share the same household, whether held individually or jointly; (ii)&nbsp;restricted stock where the restrictions have
lapsed; (iii)&nbsp;shares acquired upon stock option exercise; (iv)&nbsp;shares purchased in the open market; (v)&nbsp;restricted stock units where the restrictions have lapsed but the issuance of the shares to the director has been deferred at the
election of the director pursuant to a Company policy, plan or written agreement; and (vi)&nbsp;shares held in trust. &#147;Net shares&#148; are the number of shares from the sale of stock options or the vesting of restricted stock or restricted
stock units, less the number of shares the director sells to cover the exercise price of stock options and sells to pay taxes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As of
December&nbsp;26, 2020, all of our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors were holding the required number of shares under our stock ownership guidelines or had time remaining to do so within the established compliance time
frame. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.20em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.20em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Age: 65</P></TD></TR>
</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B>Mr.</B><B></B><B>&nbsp;Kumar</B><I> </I>is our Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer.
Mr.&nbsp;Kumar is responsible for the company&#146;s global finance organization and oversees financial management of the company as well as global corporate services and facilities. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Since joining AMD in 1984, Mr.&nbsp;Kumar has progressed through leadership positions in corporate accounting and corporate finance, including serving 10
years as the regional finance director in Asia. From 2001 to 2012, Mr.&nbsp;Kumar served as Corporate Controller. He was appointed Chief Financial Officer in January 2013 and his role was expanded to include Treasurer in April 2015. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mr.&nbsp;Kumar has served as a member of the board of directors of Ciena Corporation (a networking systems, services and software company) since August
2019. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mr.&nbsp;Kumar holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Ecology from the University of Malaya, Malaysia, a Master of Science degree in Biology
from the University of California, Santa Barbara and an MBA in Finance from the University of California, Los Angeles. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

responsible for the company&#146;s graphics and semi-custom businesses as well as combining AMD&#146;s high-performance CPUs, GPUs and software to create differentiated solutions. Mr.&nbsp;Bergman brings over 30 years of industry experience
including significant business leadership experience. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Previously, Mr.&nbsp;Bergman was president and CEO for Synaptics, a leading developer of human
interface solutions including touch, display, IoT and biometrics solutions, from October 2011 to March 2019. Prior to that, he served in a series of senior executive positions at AMD, where he was Senior Vice President and General Manager of
AMD&#146;s Product Group from May 2009 to September 2011, and Senior Vice President and General Manager of AMD&#146;s Graphics Product Group from October 2006 to May 2009. During his time at AMD, Mr.&nbsp;Bergman was responsible for delivering
microprocessors and graphics chips to our customers across server, client, embedded and game consoles, and for driving the technology that put a graphics chip and processor on a single piece of silicon. Until AMD acquired ATI Technologies Inc. in
2006, Mr.&nbsp;Bergman was Senior Vice President and General Manager of ATI Technologies&#146; PC Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Additionally, he has held senior management
positions at S3 Graphics, Texas Instruments and IBM and was a board member of Maxwell Technologies from 2015 until it was acquired by Tesla in May 2019. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mr.&nbsp;Bergman holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering from the&nbsp;University of Michigan&nbsp;and a Master of Science degree in
Business Administration from the&nbsp;University of Colorado&#146;s&nbsp;Executive MBA program. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.20em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Senior Vice President and General Manager, Datacenter and Embedded Solutions Business Group</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.20em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Age: 55</P></TD></TR>
</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B>Mr.</B><B></B><B>&nbsp;Norrod</B> is our Senior Vice President and General Manager of the Datacenter and Embedded
Solutions Business Group. In this role, he is responsible for managing all aspects of strategy, business management, engineering and sales for AMD data center and embedded products. Mr.&nbsp;Norrod joined AMD in November 2014. Mr.&nbsp;Norrod has
more than 25 years of technology industry experience across a number of engineering and business management roles at both the chip and system level. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mr.&nbsp;Norrod was Vice President and General Manager of Dell Inc.&#146;s server business from December 2009 to October 2014, driving the business to
market share leadership in several key geographies and markets while delivering consistent revenue and profitability growth. In his role as Vice President and General Manager of Dell&#146;s Data Center Solutions, Mr.&nbsp;Norrod successfully led the
creation of the company&#146;s first internal startup, which established Dell&#146;s leadership presence in the hyper-scale datacenter market. He joined Dell as CTO of Client Products in August 2000, then led the company&#146;s Enterprise
Engineering before ultimately having responsibility for all of Dell&#146;s global engineering teams. Prior to Dell, Mr.&nbsp;Norrod worked at Cyrix Corp from 1993 to 1997 and National Semiconductor from 1997 to 2000 leading the integrated x86 CPU
businesses. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mr.&nbsp;Norrod holds Bachelor of Science and Master of Science degrees in Electrical Engineering from Virginia Tech and holds 11 US
patents in computer architecture, graphics and system design. He served on the board of directors of Intersil Corporation from October 2014 until it was acquired in February 2017. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster holds a Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Texas at Austin and a Master of Science degree from the University of

</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><I>2020 Business Highlights </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">2020 marked an
inflection point in our long-term journey as we made significant progress establishing AMD as the high-performance computing leader, while setting a new record for annual revenue. We significantly accelerated our business and exceeded our aggressive
growth goals for the year while navigating industry-wide challenges caused by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19.</FONT> We built substantial momentum throughout the year as we successfully ramped volume production of more than twenty 7nm PC,
gaming, and data center products. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We made great progress across our businesses in 2020 as we gained market share with our 7nm Ryzen&#153; and
EPYC&#153; processors. For the year, record annual client processor revenue grew by more than 50&nbsp;percent as AMD Ryzen processor demand increased. Adoption of EPYC processors across cloud, enterprise and HPC customers also accelerated
significantly in 2020. We set a new <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">all-time</FONT> record for annual server processor revenue. Server processor sales more than doubled year-over-year, and our overall data center sales are now a high teens
percentage of our total annual revenue. Strong demand for our 7nm products powered by our &#147;Zen 3&#148; processor core increased AMD&#146; momentum across the PC, Gaming and data center markets </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our financial results in fiscal 2020 compared to fiscal 2019 were strong as we delivered record annual revenue, higher gross margins, and a significant
growth in profitability. In 2020, we grew revenue by 45% year-over-year to $9.76&nbsp;billion and increased our gross margin to 45% compared to 43% in the prior year, which marked our highest gross margin since 2011. We increased our operating
income to $1.37&nbsp;billion compared to $631&nbsp;million for fiscal 2019 and improved our net income to $2.49&nbsp;billion, including a $1.30&nbsp;billion income tax benefit associated with a valuation allowance release, compared to
$341&nbsp;million in the prior year. We also made significant progress strengthening our balance sheet as our cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $2.29&nbsp;billion, up from $1.50&nbsp;billion in the prior year. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">(1)</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial; " ALIGN="left">Each Named Executive Officer&#146;s &#147;realized pay&#148; is the sum of his or her earned base salary, actual annual
incentive bonus under the EIP, any discretionary or retention bonus amounts realized, other compensation, and Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-2</FONT> income realized due to stock option exercises and the vesting of restricted stock unit and
performance-based awards under our equity plans for the applicable fiscal year. Additional information is provided below in the &#147;2020 Summary Compensation Table&#148; on page&nbsp;57 and the &#147;Option Exercises and Stock Vested in 2020&#148;
table on page&nbsp;63. Realized pay is not a substitute for total compensation. For more information on total compensation as calculated under SEC rules, see the notes accompanying the 2020 Summary Compensation Table below. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:8pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

Executive Officers during those years. The fiscal 2019 average of the Other Named Executive Officers excludes Mr.&nbsp;Bergman, who joined us on August&nbsp;5, 2019. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:8pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">(3)</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial; " ALIGN="left">The AMD Market Capitalization amounts are as of the last day of each applicable fiscal year. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The realized pay of our Named Executive Officers in 2020 was primarily attributable to (i)&nbsp;the growth in AMD stock price and the vesting of
long-term equity awards and exercise of stock options that were granted in prior years, (ii)&nbsp;payout vs. target amounts for PRSUs and (iii)&nbsp;their annual incentive bonuses under the EIP. The EIP payout in 2020 was 142% of target compared to
74.6% of target in 2019 and 86% of target in 2018, resulting in an average payout under the EIP for the previous three fiscal years of 100.9% of target. For a discussion of the EIP, see &#147;2020 Compensation Elements&#151;Annual Incentive
Bonuses&#148; below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_27"></A>Response to 2020 &#147;Say On Pay&#148; Vote and Stockholder Engagement Process </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee seeks to align the objectives of our executive compensation program with the interests of our stockholders. When evaluating
our executive compensation program, the Compensation Committee carefully considers both the results of our annual advisory resolution on the compensation of our Named Executive Officers (the &#147;say on pay&#148; proposal) as well as direct
feedback from our stockholders, with whom we actively and directly engage throughout the fiscal year. After three years of consistently strong (90%+) stockholder support, our &#147;say on pay&#148; resolution received 66.9% (70.2% as calculated by
Institutional Shareholder Services) support at our 2020 annual meeting of stockholders. We believe this was primarily due to the multi-year PRSU awards granted to Dr.&nbsp;Su and Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster in 2019 (the &#147;Value Creation Equity
Awards&#148;), which were intended to be <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> awards. However, as a result, during 2020 we further intensified our stockholder engagement regarding executive compensation and other corporate governance
matters. </P>

activities and diversity and inclusion discussed above. These engagement efforts with our stockholders allow us to better understand our stockholders&#146; priorities and perspectives, and provide us with useful input concerning our corporate
strategy and our compensation and ESG practices. We actively engage with our stockholders on a year-round basis and remain active outside of proxy season. Feedback from these engagements is provided to the Board who in turn decides whether
enhancements to our company&#146;s policies and practices are required to meet stockholder expectations relating to current or new issues or emerging trends. These engagements can also affect positive change at the Company which saw AMD adopting the
&#147;Rooney Rule&#148; for Board recruitment and the public availability of our EEO-1 filings. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In 2020, we engaged with over <B><U>60%</U></B> of

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">Some stockholders expressed concern with the Value Creation Equity Awards granted to Dr.&nbsp;Su and Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster.
As we explained in our definitive proxy statement for our 2020 annual meeting of stockholders and reiterated in many of our conversations with our stockholders, the Value Creation Equity Awards were intended to be
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> awards that the Compensation Committee and the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> members of our Board approved following their review and consideration of
(i)&nbsp;Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s and Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster&#146;s unique and significant contributions to our success (ii)&nbsp;our long-term objectives and strategy, (iii)&nbsp;the potential incentive and retention value of Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s and
Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster&#146;s then-outstanding equity holdings, and (iv)&nbsp;the highly competitive marketplace for executive talent. Under their leadership, AMD has performed exceptionally well from an operational, financial and stockholder return
perspective. Since Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s promotion to Chief Executive Officer in 2014, AMD has created over $109&nbsp;billion in market capitalization for our stockholders. The Compensation Committee and
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> members of our Board determined the Value Creation Equity Awards were in the best interests of AMD and its stockholders by promoting the retention and further motivation of Dr.&nbsp;Su and
Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster, whose continued focus and dedication is vitally important to our continued growth and long-term success. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">We shared stockholder feedback with the Compensation Committee, which considers both the results of our <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">say-on-pay</FONT></FONT> vote as well as direct feedback from stockholders to align the objectives of our executive compensation program with the interests of our stockholders. As we
evaluated our compensation practices for 2020, the Compensation Committee considered the strong support we received from our stockholders for the overall design of our executive compensation program during our 2020 engagement as well as in the past.
</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">Based on stockholder feedback and considering the unique circumstances of our 2019 program, the Compensation Committee
decided to retain the overall program design, which they believe emphasizes <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pay-for-performance</FONT></FONT> and provides a competitive program that effectively retains and motivates
our Named Executive Officers while aligning with stockholder value creation. Based on stockholder feedback, no Value Creation Equity Awards were granted in 2020. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><FONT COLOR="#FFFFFF"><B>Claw-back/Recovery<BR>Rights</B></FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">We have the right to claw-back incentive-based and other compensation (including equity awards) paid or granted to an employee (including any Named Executive Officer)
in the event of certain misconduct by the employee.</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">
<TD HEIGHT="5" BGCOLOR="#007298"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="5" COLSPAN="2"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff" BGCOLOR="#007298"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><FONT COLOR="#FFFFFF"><B><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">One-year</FONT> minimum<BR>vesting period for<BR>equity awards</B></FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">Our 2004 Plan requires a minimum <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> vesting period, subject to limited exceptions such as death, disability, termination
of employment or a change in control of AMD.</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">
<TD HEIGHT="5" BGCOLOR="#007298"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="5" COLSPAN="2"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff" BGCOLOR="#007298"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><FONT COLOR="#FFFFFF"><B>Change in
control<BR>payments are &#147;double-trigger&#148; and capped</B></FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">Our change in control agreements are &#147;double-trigger&#148;, meaning payments will be made only if there is an involuntary termination of employment without cause
or constructive discharge following a change in control. Further, since March 2010 we have not and will not enter into change in control agreements that provide cash change in control payments that exceed (i)&nbsp;two times the sum of base salary
and target annual incentive bonus plus (ii)&nbsp;the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pro-rated</FONT> target annual incentive bonus for the year in which the termination of employment occurs.</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">

<TD HEIGHT="5" COLSPAN="2"></TD></TR>

<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff" BGCOLOR="#007298"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><FONT COLOR="#FFFFFF"><B>No new excise
tax<BR><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">gross-ups</FONT></B></FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">Since April 2009, we have not and will not enter into any change in control agreement or arrangement with a Named Executive Officer that provides for an excise tax <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">gross-up</FONT> payment.</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="font-size:1pt">

perquisites</B></FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="middle" STYLE="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5">We provide limited perquisites or other personal benefits to our Named Executive Officers and provide air and other travel for our Named Executive Officers for
business purposes only.</TD></TR>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_12"></A>Talent Management Focus </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Developing, motivating, retaining, and attracting talent is critical to guide and execute our strategy as well as to continue to grow our business. This
is a strong focus of our executive compensation program and the Compensation Committee. Our executive compensation program aligns with our talent objectives and our compensation decisions not only consider individual and company performance, but
also long-term potential, key retention needs and organizational succession plans. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">One of the Compensation Committee&#146;s responsibilities
described in its charter is to regularly review succession planning and talent development. The Compensation Committee at least annually reviews succession plans for the Chief Executive Officer and other senior executive positions. These reviews
occur with input from the Chief Executive Officer and our Senior Vice President, Worldwide Marketing, Human Resources and Investor Relations and our Senior Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer. The Compensation Committee also reviews
succession plans in executive session, with no members of management present. Succession planning for key executive roles consists of an assessment of internal candidates and their development plans, as well as potential external talent, while
factoring in our culture and an emphasis on diversity and inclusion. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We believe that building a diverse talent pipeline, encouraging a culture of
respect and belonging, and increasing inclusion of unique and underrepresented voices makes AMD stronger. We are focused on hiring and developing under-represented minorities and women leaders. We are proud to be led by a highly regarded Chief
Executive Officer who has earned many esteemed awards for her business and technical prowess. In 2020, Dr.&nbsp;Su received the semiconductor industry&#146;s highest honor as the 2020 recipient of the Robert N. Noyce Award. Dr.&nbsp;Su also ranked
#2 on Fortune&#146;s Businessperson of the Year list for her strategic vision and successful company turnaround. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_28"></A>Compensation

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee is supported by our Chief Executive Officer (other than with respect to her own compensation) and other members of management.

objectives and strategies. These individuals did not attend either executive sessions or portions of any meetings of the Compensation Committee or our Board where their own compensation determinations were made. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> members of our Board annually conduct a performance assessment of our Chief Executive Officer.
The Compensation Committee reviews and considers this performance assessment in making its recommendations to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> members of our Board regarding the compensation and other terms of our Chief
Executive Officer&#146;s employment. Our Chief Executive Officer does not participate in the determination of her own compensation and no management recommendation is made regarding her compensation. </P>

has the authority to engage independent advisors to assist in carrying out its responsibilities. During 2020, the Compensation Committee retained Compensia, a national compensation consulting firm, as its compensation consultant to provide
assistance on executive and director compensation matters. Compensia advised the Compensation Committee on a variety of compensation-related matters, including: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
