interest assessment of its compensation consultant. In 2020, Compensia did not provide any services to or receive any payments from us, except in its capacity as a consultant to the Compensation Committee. In March 2021, the Compensation Committee
considered whether the services provided by Compensia raised any conflicts of interest pursuant to the rules of the SEC and the listing rules of Nasdaq and concluded that the work performed by Compensia did not raise any conflicts of interest. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In the course of its engagement, Compensia attended meetings of the Compensation Committee and, where applicable, presented its findings and
recommendations for discussion. Compensia also consulted frequently with members of the Compensation Committee and met with members of senior management to obtain and validate market data, review materials, and discuss management&#146;s compensation
recommendations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Role of the Chief Executive Officer </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Generally, during the Compensation Committee&#146;s annual review of executive compensation, our Chief Executive Officer reviews with the Compensation
Committee her performance evaluations of each of our other Named Executive Officers and her compensation recommendations for those Named Executive Officers. The Compensation Committee considers these recommendations in its decision process. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">
&#147;competitive market&#148; with respect to current executive compensation levels and related policies and practices. The Compensation Committee then evaluates how our pay practices and our
Named Executive Officers&#146; compensation levels compared to the competitive market. As part of this evaluation, the Compensation Committee also reviews the performance measures and related performance target levels generally used within the
competitive market to reward performance. The Compensation Committee believes that it appropriately sets the compensation of our Named Executive Officers, while taking into account the practices of our peers and industry best practices. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Methodology Used to Perform the Competitive Pay Analysis </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">To
assist the Compensation Committee in its review of the 2020 compensation for our Named Executive Officers, Compensia provided a competitive pay analysis in February 2020, which set forth compensation data developed from publicly available
information (as of November 2019) of the companies included in a custom peer group (the &#147;2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group&#148;). In May 2020, Compensia provided the Compensation Committee an update to this competitive pay analysis that
reflected, in relevant part, (a) AMD and peer stock price and financial data as of April&nbsp;17, 2020 and (b) the February&nbsp;25, 2020 retention equity award to Mr. Grasby. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">To develop the 2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group, the Compensation Committee reviewed the group of companies comprising the then-existing
compensation peer group in November 2019, with particular reference to their industry (i.e., business segment), revenues (generally 50% to 200% of our revenues for the trailing four fiscal quarters) and market capitalization (generally 30% to 300%
of our market capitalization), in each case based on publicly available information as of November&nbsp;4, 2019. The Compensation Committee selected these two metrics because, based on Compensia&#146;s analysis and holding all other factors
constant, revenue has the greatest correlation to cash compensation levels and market capitalization has the greatest influence on equity compensation levels. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on this review, the Compensation Committee removed ON Semiconductor Corp. because its market capitalization was less than 30% of our market
capitalization, and Symantec Corporation because it was undergoing major business changes and completed the sale of its enterprise security assets on November&nbsp;4, 2019. Also based on this review, and in order to improve the statistical sampling
of the peer group, the Compensation Committee added Micron Technology, Inc. and Qualcomm Inc., each of which fit within the applicable criteria for industry and market capitalization. Although Micron Technology, Inc. and Qualcomm Inc. each have
revenues that exceed 200% of our revenues for the trailing four fiscal quarters, the Compensation Committee determined it was appropriate to include them in our 2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group given the limited alternatives. Our revenues for
the trailing four fiscal quarters ending December&nbsp;28, 2019, would have placed us in approximately the 38<SUP STYLE="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">th</SUP> percentile of the 2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group based on publicly available
information. The Compensation Committee believes that the composition of the 2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group reflects an appropriate set of comparator companies for purposes of assessing our executive compensation program. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee used the 2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group competitive pay analysis developed by Compensia as its reference source in
analyzing the competitiveness of our Named Executive Officers&#146; compensation. As compared to the 2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group, AMD&#146;s fiscal 2020 and fiscal 2019 annual revenue was approximately $9.76&nbsp;billion and
$6.73&nbsp;billion, respectively. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><I>Annual Cash Performance Bonuses </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Generally, short-term
incentives in the form of an annual cash performance bonus are provided to our Named Executive Officers under the EIP. These bonuses are designed to reward short-term performance and the achievement of the principal goals of our annual operating
plan. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Under the fiscal 2020 EIP, the amount of each Named Executive Officer&#146;s annual cash performance bonus was calculated based on
(i)&nbsp;his or her target annual cash performance bonus opportunity, (ii)&nbsp;our corporate financial performance (weighted 80%) for fiscal 2020, as measured against <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-established</FONT> performance levels (the
&#147;Financial Performance Targets&#148;) and (iii)&nbsp;achievement of strategic milestones (weighted 20%) established with respect to new product tape outs, launches, and commercial/operational metrics (the &#147;Strategic Milestones&#148;). The
Financial Performance Targets and the Strategic Milestones were approved by the Compensation Committee in February 2020. Notwithstanding achievement of the fiscal 2020 performance goals, the Compensation Committee has discretion under the EIP to
increase or to reduce any Named Executive Officer&#146;s annual cash performance bonus. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The following illustrates how the 2020 annual cash
performance bonuses under the EIP were calculated: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The performance levels (threshold, target and maximum)<B> </B>for each financial performance measure were established by
the Compensation Committee in February 2020, in each case in consultation with senior management. The performance levels were structured to align with our fiscal 2020 financial objectives taking into account overall affordability of the bonus
opportunities provided under the EIP for fiscal 2020. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee chose adjusted <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> net
income as a performance measure because it is a fair measure of our profitability and a valid metric for comparison, which the Compensation Committee believes is directly tied to enhanced<B> </B>stock price performance. The Compensation Committee
assigned it a weight of 50% because it is a key short-term financial measure for the operation of our business and is a measure of significant importance to our stockholders. For purposes of the fiscal 2020 EIP, our &#147;adjusted <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> net income&#148; was calculated by adjusting our fiscal 2020 GAAP net income for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(i)&nbsp;non-GAAP</FONT> financial adjustments such as a loss on debt redemption/conversion,
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</FONT> interest expense related to convertible debt, stock-based compensation, acquisition-related costs, provision for income taxes associated with these adjustments and release of valuation allowance on
deferred tax assets, and (ii)&nbsp;amounts accrued for fiscal 2020 annual cash performance bonuses. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee chose revenue as a
performance measure because it reflects our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">top-line</FONT> growth, which the Compensation Committee believes is a strong indicator of our long-term ability to increase profitability, cash flow and improve stock
price performance. For purposes of the fiscal 2020 EIP, we use our GAAP net revenue for fiscal 2020. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Finally, the Compensation Committee chose
adjusted free cash flow as a performance measure because it believes effective cash management and cash generation are key components of our strategy and our annual operating plan, the successful execution of which should lower indebtedness,
increase financial flexibility and ultimately drive improved company valuation and stock price performance. For purposes of the fiscal 2020 EIP, our &#147;adjusted free cash flow&#148; was calculated by adjusting our GAAP net cash provided by
operating activities for (i)&nbsp;purchases of property and equipment and (ii)&nbsp;cash payments for fiscal 2019 bonuses which were paid in March and April 2020. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Strategic Milestones </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For the Strategic Milestones, which account for 20% of the EIP Performance Factor, the Compensation Committee selected (a)&nbsp;new product tape outs and
launches tied to specified internal targeted delivery dates and (b)&nbsp;achievement of various commercial/operations milestones relating to objectives for product yields and quality, inventory, brand awareness, and commercial pipeline development.
Each of the specific Strategic Milestones is confidential, the disclosure of which would cause us competitive harm. When approved, the Compensation Committee believed that each Strategic Milestone was challenging, yet reasonably achievable. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on our performance relative to the Financial Performance Targets and Strategic Milestones, the fiscal 2020 EIP reached 147% achievement. Based on
management&#146;s request to allocate a portion of the EIP funding towards a discretionary end of year cash bonus for all employees below the level of Corporate Vice President, the Compensation Committee exercised its discretion under the plan to
modify achievement from 147% to 142%. At the end of fiscal 2020, our Chief Executive Officer assessed each Named Executive Officer&#146;s performance, except her own, and made bonus recommendations to the Compensation Committee for each of them. The
Compensation Committee then considered the Chief Executive Officer&#146;s individual performance reviews and bonus recommendations, and independently assessed the company&#146;s performance and the individual performance of the Chief Executive
Officer and each of the other Named Executive Officers. Based on its assessment of each of these factors and considering the company&#146;s strong performance relative to the Financial Performance Targets and Strategic Milestones, the Compensation
Committee approved fiscal 2020 annual cash performance bonuses under the EIP for the Named Executive Officers as set forth below: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In approving the aggregate intended target value of each Named Executive Officer&#146;s 2020 annual long-term equity award, the Compensation Committee
(the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> members of our Board for Dr.&nbsp;Su) reviewed data showing the market-competitive award levels based on the 2020 Executive Compensation Peer Group and the potential realizable value of
each Named Executive Officer&#146;s then-outstanding equity holdings. Additionally, the Compensation Committee (the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-management</FONT> members of our Board for Dr.&nbsp;Su) considered the potential realizable
value of each Named Executive Officer&#146;s then-outstanding equity holdings, our executive retention objectives and continuity within senior management and the following high-level corporate goals: achieve fiscal 2020 financial results, execute
industry-leading roadmap and meet customer commitments. The achievement of these high-level goals drive our overall Company business strategy and, correspondingly, the attainment of the performance objectives in our long-term incentive compensation
program. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>2020 Annual PRSU Awards.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2020 annual PRSU awards (the &#147;2020 Annual PRSUs&#148;) provide for a payout that will

Executive Officer will be reduced to 50% of his or her Adjusted Earned Shares. If the return on our stock price over the Performance Period is equal to or greater than zero percent, then the total number of shares earned by each Named Executive
Officer will be the number of his or her Adjusted Earned Shares. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Any PRSUs that are earned will generally be settled on the later
of August&nbsp;16, 2023, or the date following the Compensation Committee&#146;s certification of our performance achievement. Each Named Executive Officer must be continuously employed through the last day of the Performance Period to receive his
or her earned shares, except to the extent an event triggers accelerated vesting of the 2020 Annual PRSUs under the terms of his or her employment or other agreement, as applicable. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Stock Options</I>.&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock options are intended to align the interests of our Named Executive Officers with the interests of our stockholders
because they will not realize any financial benefit from these awards unless our stock price increases above the exercise price over the seven-year option term. The stock options have an exercise price equal to 100% of the fair market value of our
common stock on the grant date, which was $84.85 per share. The stock options vest (and become exercisable) as to 33 <SUP STYLE="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">1</SUP>/<SUB STYLE="font-size:85%; vertical-align:bottom">3</SUB>% of the underlying
shares on each of August&nbsp;9, 2021, August&nbsp;9, 2022 and August&nbsp;9, 2023, subject to each Named Executive Officer&#146;s continued employment with us through each vesting date (unless his or her employment agreement or other agreement with
us provides otherwise). The service-based vesting requirements are intended to further our retention objectives. The stock options expire seven years after the grant date, subject to earlier expiration if the Named Executive Officer&#146;s
employment with us terminates. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>RSUs</I>.&nbsp;&nbsp;RSUs are intended to encourage executive retention, manage share dilution, recognize
individual performance and align the interests of our Named Executive Officers with our stockholders because the value of the awards is tied to the market value of our common stock at the time of vesting. All of the RSUs granted to our Named
Executive Officers in 2020 vest as to 33<SUP STYLE="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top"> 1</SUP>/<SUB STYLE="font-size:85%; vertical-align:bottom">3</SUB>% of the underlying shares on each of August&nbsp;9, 2021, August&nbsp;9, 2022 and
August&nbsp;9, 2023, subject to each Named Executive Officer&#146;s continued employment with us through each vesting date (unless his or her employment agreement or other agreement with us provides otherwise). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Retention Equity Award &#150; Darren Grasby </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In February 2020,
the Compensation Committee approved the grant of a retention equity award to Mr.&nbsp;Grasby having a target value of $4&nbsp;million. The award was in recognition of his unique and significant contributions to our fiscal 2019 performance and to
encourage his retention through 2023. The target value of the retention equity award was converted into a mix of 50% PRSUs and 50% time-based RSUs, which were granted on February&nbsp;15, 2020 under the terms of the 2004 Plan. The PRSUs have the
same performance and service vesting conditions as the PRSUs granted on August&nbsp;9, 2019 to our fiscal 2019 Named Executive Officers and which are described in detail in our definitive proxy statement for our 2020 annual meeting of stockholders
filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on March&nbsp;26, 2020. The time-based RSUs vest in three equal annual installments on each of the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Accounting Considerations </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We follow ASC Topic 718 for our
share-based compensation awards. ASC Topic 718 requires companies to measure the compensation expense for all share-based payment awards made to employees and directors, including stock options, based on the grant date &#147;fair value&#148; of
these awards. This calculation is performed for accounting purposes and reported in the compensation tables below, even though our Named Executive Officers may never realize any value from their awards. ASC Topic 718 also requires companies to
recognize the compensation cost of their share-based compensation awards in their income statements over the period that a recipient is required to render service in exchange for the option or other award. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In accordance with ASC Topic 718, the accounting value of the 2020 Annual PRSUs and the retention PRSUs to Mr.&nbsp;Grasby were calculated by an outside
professional valuation consultant using a Monte-Carlo simulation model and based upon a discounted cash flow analysis of the probability-weighted payoffs of a share-based payment assuming a variety of possible stock price paths and represents the
estimate of aggregate compensation cost to be recognized over the requisite service period determined as of the grant date under ASC Topic 718, except no assumptions for forfeitures are included. The amounts reported in the 2020 Summary Compensation
Table include the grant date fair values (i.e., accounting values) of the awards. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><I>Termination of Employment Required to Trigger Payments </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Under the terms and conditions of these change in control agreements and the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">change-in-control</FONT></FONT> provisions of Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s employment agreement, each of our Named Executive Officers is eligible to receive certain specified payments and
benefits only if (a)&nbsp;a &#147;change in control&#148; of us occurs and (b)&nbsp;the Named Executive Officer&#146;s employment is terminated or the Named Executive Officer is constructively discharged within two years of the change in control
transaction (a &#147;double trigger&#148; arrangement). The Compensation Committee believes this structure strikes a balance between our incentive arrangements and our executive hiring and retention objectives without providing &#147;windfall&#148;
payments and benefits to any Named Executive Officers who continue employment with an acquiring entity following a change in control of AMD. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For a

in Control Arrangements&#148; section on page&nbsp;65 below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_31"></A>Severance and Separation Arrangements </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Any post-employment compensation payable to our Chief Executive Officer is governed solely by her employment agreement, the terms of which were the
result of arms-length negotiations between her and the Compensation Committee. Under her employment agreement, Dr.&nbsp;Su is eligible to receive certain specified payments and benefits in the event that her employment is involuntarily terminated.
The Compensation Committee believes that the amount payable to Dr.&nbsp;Su pursuant to her employment agreement is reasonable and competitive and provides transition assistance in the event of her involuntary termination of employment, with the goal
of keeping her focused on our business rather than her personal circumstances. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">With the exception of our Chief Executive Officer, all of our other
Named Executive Officers participate in our Executive Severance Plan for Executive Vice Presidents and Senior Vice Presidents (the &#147;Executive Severance Plan&#148;). The Executive Severance Plan is designed to provide uniform treatment in the
event of an involuntary termination of employment of our U.S. senior executives (except our Chief Executive Officer) and to provide transition assistance in such instances with the goal of keeping these senior executives focused on our business
rather than their personal circumstances. A Named Executive Officer is not eligible to receive payments and benefits under the Executive Severance Plan if he or she receives severance payments and benefits in connection with a change in control of
AMD pursuant to his or her change in control agreement. The Compensation Committee believes that the Executive Severance Plan provides the covered executives important protections and promotes our objectives of attracting and retaining executive
talent. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For a detailed description of the post-employment compensation arrangements of our Named Executive Officers, as well as an estimate of the

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_32"></A>Other Compensation Policies </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Compensation
Recovery (&#147;Claw-back&#148;) Rights </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct provide that we may pursue all remedies available under
applicable law to recover any incentive-based or other compensation (including equity awards) paid or granted to our employees or agents in the event of such individual&#146;s direct involvement with fraud, misconduct or gross negligence which
contributes to an accounting restatement as a result of our material noncompliance with any financial reporting laws. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In addition, the award
agreement for each stock option, RSU, and PRSU granted since May 2010 to an employee at or above the level of senior vice president (which includes our Named Executive Officers) has included a compensation recoupment (&#147;claw-back&#148;)
provision. The claw-back provides the Compensation Committee with the right to recover all or a portion of the compensation attributable to the award if the employee&#146;s direct involvement with fraud, misconduct or his or her gross negligence
contributes to or results in us being required to prepare an accounting restatement as a result of our material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under the federal<B> </B>securities laws. The claw-back does not apply to any
award granted more than 18 months before the date of the first public issuance or SEC filing of the financial document embodying the reporting requirement. In addition, </P>

Ownership Requirements </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our stock ownership requirements are designed to increase our Named Executive Officers&#146; stakes in us and to align
their interests more closely with those of our stockholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In August 2020, we increased our stock ownership requirements for our Named Executive
Officers. These requirements provide that on or before the Ownership Achievement Date (as defined below), our Chief Executive Officer should attain an investment position in our common stock equal to the lesser of
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(a)&nbsp;six-times</FONT> her then-current annual base salary or (b) 350,000 shares, and our other Named Executive Officers should attain an investment position in our common stock equal to the lesser of (x) 2.5
times their then-current annual base salaries or (y) 80,000 shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Shares of our common stock counted toward the minimum stock ownership
requirements include any shares held directly or indirectly by a Named Executive Officer. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The &#147;Ownership Achievement Date&#148; is the later of
August&nbsp;7, 2025, or five years from first appointment as an executive officer. Until the guideline is achieved, each Named Executive Officer is encouraged to retain at least 10% of the net shares (defined below) obtained through our stock
incentive plans. For this purpose, the &#147;net shares&#148; are the number of shares received from the exercise of stock options or the vesting of restricted stock or restricted stock unit awards, less the number of shares the Named Executive
Officer sells to cover the exercise price of stock options or sells or has withheld to pay taxes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As of December&nbsp;26, 2020, each of our Named
Executive Officers had satisfied his or her applicable stock ownership requirement or has time remaining to do so. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B>Deductibility of Executive Compensation
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Section&nbsp;162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code (&#147;Code&#148;) generally disallows public companies a tax deduction for federal income tax
purposes of remuneration in excess of $1&nbsp;million paid to certain executive officers. While the Compensation Committee may consider the deductibility of awards as one factor in determining our executive compensation, it also considers other
factors in making its executive compensation decisions and retains the flexibility to grant awards or pay compensation the Compensation Committee determines to be consistent with its goals for our executive compensation program, even if the awards
may not be deductible for tax purposes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act repealed the exception to the deductibility limit that was previously available
for &#147;qualified performance-based compensation&#148; (including stock option grants, performance-based cash bonuses and performance-based equity awards, such as the PRSUs) effective for taxable years beginning after December&nbsp;31, 2017. As a
result, any compensation paid to certain of our Named Executive Officers for taxable years beginning after December&nbsp;31, 2017 in excess of $1&nbsp;million will be <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-deductible</FONT> unless it qualifies for
transition relief afforded by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act to compensation payable pursuant to certain binding arrangements in effect on November&nbsp;2, 2017 and which are not subsequently materially modified. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_34"></A>COMPENSATION POLICIES AND PRACTICES </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In February&nbsp;2020, the Compensation Committee reviewed our compensation policies and practices for employees generally and concluded that these
policies and practices do not create risks that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on us. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In reaching this conclusion, the
Compensation Committee, with the assistance of management, assessed our executive and broad-based compensation and benefits programs to determine if any of them created undesired or excessive risks of a material nature. The assessment included
(i)&nbsp;a review of our compensation policies and practices for employees generally, (ii)&nbsp;identification of the risks that could result from such policies and practices, (iii)&nbsp;identification of the risk mitigators and controls, and
(iv)&nbsp;analysis of the potential risks against the risk mitigators and controls and our business strategy and objectives. Although the Compensation Committee reviewed our compensation programs, the Compensation Committee focused on the programs
that have variability of payout and in which employees could directly affect the payout of incentives. These programs included the EIP, Annual Incentive Plan, Long-Term Incentive Plan (&#147;LTI&#148;), Sales Incentive Plan and 2004 Plan. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In performing the assessment and reaching its conclusion, the Compensation Committee noted the following factors that the Compensation Committee believes
may reduce the likelihood of undesired or excessive risk-taking: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="5%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">Our overall compensation levels are competitive with the market; </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="5%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">Our compensation practices and policies appropriately balance base pay versus variable pay and short-term versus long-term
incentives; </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="5%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">Although the EIP, Annual Incentive Plan, LTI and Sales Incentive Plan have variability of payout, the Compensation
Committee believes that any potential risks associated with such plans are controlled or mitigated by one or more of the following: (i)&nbsp;the performance goals being multi-dimensional (i.e., adjusted
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> net income, adjusted <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> free cash flow, revenue), thereby increasing the range of performance over which incentives are paid; (ii)&nbsp;the performance
goals being aligned with our business objectives and being quantitative financial measures; (iii)&nbsp;the use of sliding payout scales, with the payouts in certain instances being linearly interpolated for performance falling between the
performance levels set by the Compensation Committee; (iv)&nbsp;the ability of the Compensation Committee and/or management to exercise discretion to reduce payouts; (v)&nbsp;the existence of multiple internal controls and approval processes that
are intended to prevent manipulation of outcomes by any employee, including the Named Executive Officers; and (vi)&nbsp;the incentive opportunities being capped; </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="5%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">Although the grant of equity awards under the 2004 Plan could motivate our employees to, among other things, focus on
increasing our short-term stock price rather than the creation of long-term stockholder value, the Compensation Committee believes that potential risks are controlled or mitigated by one or more of the following: (i)&nbsp;awarding a combination of
PRSUs, RSUs and stock options; (ii)&nbsp;three-year vesting and performance period for PRSUs awarded in fiscal 2019 and 2020 (with the exception of the Value Creation Equity Awards granted in fiscal 2019, which have a five-year performance period);
(iii)&nbsp;the vesting provisions of stock options and RSUs occurring over multi-year periods, (iv)&nbsp;caps on performance-based compensation opportunities; and (v)&nbsp;our stock ownership guidelines for our executive officers. In addition, we
prohibit our employees, including Named Executive Officers, from engaging in hedging transactions in our securities; and </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">We have implemented claw-back provisions and policies, as described in more detail in &#147;Compensation Discussion and
Analysis&#148; above. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial; " ALIGN="left">Mr.&nbsp;Bergman&#146;s balance includes $199,922 that was reported as compensation in the &#147;Summary Compensation

maintain the DIA, which allows eligible employees, including the Named Executive Officers, to voluntarily defer receipt of a portion of their salary, bonus and any commission payments until the date or dates selected by the participant. Participants
may defer up to 50% of annual base salary and/or 100% of commissions and bonuses. Earnings on the deferred accounts are based on the performance of the investment funds selected by the participants. Participants make a deferral election, prior to
the year in which the compensation is earned, that may not be terminated or changed during the year for which it was made. Generally, we make a discretionary contribution to the participant&#146;s account if his or her annual base salary, minus his
or her Section&nbsp;401(k) contribution before the deferral, is greater than the annual compensation limit for Section&nbsp;401(k) plans. The contribution, if any, is equal to the lesser of (i)&nbsp;50% of the deferred compensation credited to the
participant&#146;s account for the year or (ii)&nbsp;a discretionary percentage of the participant&#146;s base salary in excess of the eligible Section&nbsp;401(k) compensation limit for the year minus the participant&#146;s Section&nbsp;401(k)
contributions. For 2020, our discretionary contribution percentage under option (ii)&nbsp;above was 4.5%. Participants are 100% vested in the value of their accounts. Participants may select their desired benchmark investment fund(s) in which their
accounts are deemed to be invested and may change their investment elections at any time, with such change effective as of the next business day. The amount of investment gain or loss that is credited to the participant&#146;s account depends on the
participant&#146;s investment election. For 2020, we utilized investment funds in an array of asset classes, substantially aligned to those offered under our Section&nbsp;401(k) plan. We have placed assets in mutual funds held in a Rabbi trust
established for the DIA. For 2020, the investment return credited to Messrs.&nbsp;Kumar&#146;s, Bergman&#146;s and Papermaster&#146;s DIA accounts was 23.0%, 41.7%, and 7.8%, respectively, based on their investment elections for their respective DIA
accounts. This investment return was calculated by taking the aggregate gain in fiscal 2020 and dividing it by the aggregate balance as of the beginning of fiscal 2020. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The DIA accounts are distributed following a participant&#146;s termination of employment with us unless the participant has elected an <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-service</FONT> withdrawal (scheduled or hardship withdrawal). At the time a participant makes his or her deferral election, he or she may elect a different form of distribution for such year&#146;s deferred
compensation. The participant may elect a single lump sum distribution or annual installment distributions over three to ten years. The default form of distribution is a single lump sum. A participant may change the form of distribution election,
subject to the terms of the DIA. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">A participant may elect to withdraw all or part of his or her account while employed by us, subject to the terms of
the DIA. The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-service</FONT> withdrawal date must be at least two years after the plan year in which the election was made. An <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-service</FONT> withdrawal date may be changed,
subject to the terms of the DIA. An unscheduled payment may also be made, subject to the terms of the DIA. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_41"></A>SEVERANCE AND CHANGE IN CONTROL ARRANGEMENTS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We have entered into an employment agreement with Dr.&nbsp;Su, our current President and Chief Executive Officer. In addition, Messrs. Kumar, Bergman,
Grasby and Papermaster participate in the Executive Severance Plan and have each entered into a change in control agreement with us. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Executive
Severance Plan and change in control agreements are designed to (i)&nbsp;implement a uniform process for handling potential future involuntary departures of the Named Executive Officers, and (ii)&nbsp;encourage the Named Executive Officers&#146;
continued services in the event of a potential change in control of us and to allow for a smooth transition upon such a change in control. In addition, these arrangements are intended to provide incentives to the Named Executive Officers to
effectively execute the directives of our Board, even in the event that such actions may result in the elimination of a Named Executive Officer&#146;s position. Under the terms of the change in control agreements, a Named Executive Officer is
eligible to receive certain specified compensatory payments and benefits only if (i)&nbsp;a &#147;change in control&#148; occurs, and (ii)&nbsp;the Named Executive Officer&#146;s employment is terminated, or the Named Executive Officer is
constructively discharged, within two years of that change in control. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Dr.</I><I></I><I>&nbsp;Su&#146;s Employment
Agreement.</I><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</I>Pursuant to Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-will</FONT> employment agreement (the &#147;Su Employment Agreement&#148;), setting forth Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s duties and obligations as
our President and Chief Executive Officer, the Su Employment Agreement may be terminated by (i)&nbsp;us for Cause (as defined in the Su Employment Agreement), (ii)&nbsp;Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s Involuntary Termination Without Cause (as defined in the Su
Employment Agreement), (iii)&nbsp;Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s Constructive Termination (as defined in the Su Employment Agreement), (iv)&nbsp;Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s voluntary election to terminate her employment with us, or (v)&nbsp;Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s death or
disability. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Except as otherwise described in the next paragraph, in the event of Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s Involuntary Termination Without Cause or
Constructive Termination, subject to Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s execution of a full release of claims, which remains effective, following such termination: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

enter into any new change in control agreements or arrangements containing an excise tax <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">gross-up</FONT> provision. Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s change in control agreement does not provide for an excise tax <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">gross-up.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In March 2010, we also adopted a policy to not enter into any new change in control agreement or
arrangement with any executive officer that provides for a cash severance payment (upon both our change in control and a subsequent termination of employment) in excess of (i)&nbsp;two times the sum of the respective executive officer&#146;s base
salary and annual target bonus, plus (ii)&nbsp;a prorated annual target bonus for the year in which the termination of employment occurs. Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s change in control agreement complies with this limitation. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><I>Vesting of Awards.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;All RSUs and stock options granted under our equity incentive plans become fully vested (i)&nbsp;if our
successor refuses to assume or substitute similar awards for outstanding awards, upon a change in control, or (ii)&nbsp;if our successor assumes or substitutes similar awards for outstanding awards and the participant&#146;s employment is terminated
by our successor for any reason (other than for misconduct) or by the participant due to a constructive termination within one year following a change in control, upon such termination of employment. All PRSUs vest to the extent the applicable
performance criteria were achieved. Upon a change in control, the Compensation Committee shall determine and approve the Company&#146;s performance with respect to the applicable performance vesting conditions as of the effective date of the change
in control and the participant will be deemed to have earned that number of PRSUs, which will be converted automatically into an equal number of RSUs that will vest as of the first to occur of (i)&nbsp;the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> anniversary of the change in control or (ii)&nbsp;the last day of the originally scheduled performance period. All remaining unearned PRSUs will be automatically forfeited without consideration. If
the participant&#146;s employment or service with the Company is involuntarily terminated for any reason (other than misconduct) after a change in control, then all such converted RSUs will become fully vested as of the date of termination. Upon
death or disability, the participant or the participant&#146;s estate shall have the right for a period of twelve (12)&nbsp;months following the date of death or termination of status as a service provider to exercise any stock options to the extent
the participant was entitled to exercise such stock options on the date of death or termination. For the Value Creation Equity Awards, if Dr.&nbsp;Su incurs a &#147;covered termination&#148; (as defined in her employment agreement) or if
Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster&#146;s employment with the Company is involuntarily terminated (other than for misconduct) during the performance period, then (a)&nbsp;the unvested earned Value Creation Equity Awards held by Dr.&nbsp;Su or
Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster, as applicable, that were scheduled to vest on or before the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> anniversary of the termination date will immediately vest and (b)&nbsp;the unvested unearned Value Creation Equity
Awards held by Dr.&nbsp;Su or Mr.&nbsp;Papermaster, as applicable, will remain outstanding for 12 months (or, if earlier, until August&nbsp;9, 2024 or the date of a change in control) and vest if such Value Creation Equity Awards would have vested
had he or she remained employed in a covered position for such period. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_42"></A>CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER PAY&nbsp;RATIO </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For 2020: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">the annual total compensation for the median employee of the Company (other than our Chief Executive Officer) was $118,959;

<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

total compensation of our Chief Executive Officer to the annual total compensation of the median employee was 228 to 1. This ratio is a reasonable estimate calculated in a manner consistent with Item 402(u) of Regulation <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">S-K</FONT> under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. As permitted by SEC rules, to identify our median employee, we selected total estimated compensation which we calculated as annual base pay plus the target bonus plus
the intended value of stock awards, as the compensation measure to be used to compare the total estimated compensation of our employees as of December 1, 2020. We annualized base pay and estimated bonus for any regular employees who commenced work
during 2020 and did not annualize these amounts for temporary and seasonal employees. The annual total compensation of the median employee and the annual total compensation of the CEO were calculated in accordance with the requirements of Item
402(c)(2)(x) of Regulation <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">S-K,</FONT> and the median employee&#146;s annual total compensation was converted to U.S. dollars using a currency exchange rate as of December 26, 2020. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_43"></A>CERTAIN RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Audit and Finance Committee monitors and reviews issues involving potential conflicts of interest and related party transactions. In doing so, the
Audit and Finance Committee applies our Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct, which provides that directors, Named Executive Officers and all other employees are expected to avoid any relationship, influence or activity that would cause or even
appear to cause a conflict of interest. Our Governance Principles require a director to promptly disclose to the Chairman of the Board any conflict of interest involving the director. In fiscal 2020, we did not conduct any transactions with related
persons that would require disclosure pursuant to applicable SEC rules. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_44"></A>AUDIT AND FINANCE COMMITTEE&#146;S REPORT </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Audit and Finance Committee consists of Mr.&nbsp;Householder, as Chair, and Messrs. Caldwell, Gregoire and Marren. Each of the members of the Audit
and Finance Committee is &#147;independent&#148; and &#147;financially literate,&#148; as determined by the Board and in compliance with SEC and Nasdaq rules. In addition, Mr.&nbsp;Householder was determined to be an &#147;audit committee financial
expert,&#148; as that term is defined under SEC rules. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Audit and Finance Committee oversees our internal audit function and independent
registered public accounting firm and assists the Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibilities on matters relating to the integrity of AMD&#146;s financial statements and the effectiveness of AMD&#146;s internal control over financial
reporting, AMD&#146;s compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, the performance of our internal audit function and the independent registered public accounting firm&#146;s qualifications, independence and performance by meeting regularly
with the independent registered public accounting firm, our senior management and our internal audit, financial, and legal personnel. Management is responsible for the preparation, presentation and integrity of AMD&#146;s financial statements and
maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting. The independent registered public accounting firm is responsible for performing an audit of AMD&#146;s annual financial statements and of the effectiveness of AMD&#146;s internal
control over financial reporting and expressing opinions on both in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In fulfilling its oversight responsibilities, the Audit and Finance Committee reviewed and discussed AMD&#146;s audited financial statements for the
fiscal year ended December&nbsp;26, 2020 with management and Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP, AMD&#146;s independent registered public accounting firm. The Audit and Finance Committee also discussed with Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP the matters required to
be discussed by the applicable requirements of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board and the SEC. This included a discussion of the independent registered public accounting firm&#146;s judgments as to the quality, not just the acceptability,
of AMD&#146;s accounting principles and such other matters that generally accepted auditing standards require to be discussed with the Audit and Finance Committee. The Audit and Finance Committee also received the written disclosures and the letter
from Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP required by the applicable requirements of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board regarding the independent accountant&#146;s communications with the audit committee concerning independence, and the Audit
Committee discussed the independence of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP with that firm. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on the Audit and Finance Committee&#146;s review and
discussions noted above, the Audit and Finance Committee recommended to the Board, and the Board approved, that the audited financial statements be included in AMD&#146;s Annual Report on Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10-K</FONT> for the
fiscal year ended December&nbsp;26, 2020 for filing with the SEC. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Audit and Finance Committee and the Board also have recommended, subject to
stockholder ratification, the selection of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as AMD&#146;s independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal 2021. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV ALIGN="right">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_45"></A>ITEM&nbsp;2&#151;RATIFICATION OF THE APPOINTMENT OF THE INDEPENDENT
REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Audit and Finance Committee is responsible for the appointment, compensation, retention and oversight of
the work of our independent registered public accounting firm. The Audit and Finance Committee has selected Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as our independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2021 and has further directed that management
submit the selection of the independent registered public accounting firm for ratification by our stockholders at the annual meeting. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Although
ratification by our stockholders is not a prerequisite to the Audit and Finance Committee&#146;s ability to select Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as our independent registered public accounting firm, the Audit and Finance Committee believes such
ratification is advisable and in the best interests of our stockholders. Accordingly, stockholders are being requested to ratify, confirm and approve the selection of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as our independent registered public accounting firm to
conduct the annual audit of our consolidated financial statements and our internal control over financial reporting for the current fiscal year. If the stockholders do not ratify the selection of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP, the selection of our
independent registered public accounting firm will be reconsidered by the Audit and Finance Committee; provided, however, the Audit and Finance Committee may select Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP notwithstanding the failure of our stockholders to ratify
its selection. If the appointment of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP is ratified, the Audit and Finance Committee will continue to conduct an ongoing review of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP&#146;s scope of engagement, pricing and work quality, among other
factors, and will retain the right to replace Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP at any time. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Unless you vote otherwise, your proxy will vote <B>FOR</B> the
ratification of the appointment of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for the current fiscal year. The Audit and Finance Committee meets with Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP several times a year. A
representative of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP is expected to be present at our Annual Meeting and will have an opportunity to make a statement if he or she so desires. He or she will also be available to respond to appropriate questions from
stockholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_46"></A>Required Vote </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Ratification of the appointment of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as our independent registered public accounting firm requires the affirmative vote of a
majority of the shares of our common stock entitled to vote and present in person or represented by proxy at our Annual Meeting. Abstentions have the same effect as a vote against this proposal. Because brokers and other nominees have discretionary
authority to vote on the ratification, we do not expect any broker <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-votes</FONT> in connection with this item. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_47">
</A>Recommendation of the Board of Directors </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B>The Board of Directors unanimously recommends that you vote FOR the ratification of the
appointment of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP as our independent registered public accounting firm for the current year. Unless you vote otherwise, your proxy will vote FOR ratification. </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><B><A NAME="toc85905_49"></A>Pre-Approval Policies and Procedures </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Audit and Finance Committee Charter provides that the Audit and Finance Committee must <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approve</FONT> the
engagement before an independent registered public accounting firm is engaged by us or our subsidiaries to render audit or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</FONT> services. Audit and Finance Committee
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approval</FONT> of audit and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</FONT> services is not required if the engagement for the services is entered into pursuant to
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approval</FONT> policies and procedures established by the Audit and Finance Committee regarding our engagement of the independent registered public accounting firm, provided the policies and procedures are
detailed as to the particular service, the committee is informed of each service provided and such policies and procedures do not include delegation to our management of the committee&#146;s responsibilities under the Securities Exchange Act of
1934, as amended. The Audit and Finance Committee may delegate to one or more designated members of the committee the authority to grant <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approvals,</FONT> provided such approvals are presented to the committee at
a subsequent meeting. If the Audit and Finance Committee elects to establish <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approval</FONT> policies and procedures regarding <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</FONT> services, the Audit and Finance
Committee must be informed of each <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</FONT> service provided by the independent auditor. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our Audit and
Finance Committee reviews both audit and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</FONT> services performed by Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP and the fees charged for such services on at least an annual basis. Among other things, the Audit and Finance
Committee examines the effect that the performance of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</FONT> services may have upon the independence of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP. All services provided by Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP in fiscal 2020 and
fiscal 2019 were <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-approved</FONT> by the Audit and Finance Committee after review of each of the services proposed for approval. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="toc85905_50"></A>ITEM&nbsp;3&#151;APPROVAL ON A
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">NON-BINDING,</FONT> ADVISORY BASIS OF THE COMPENSATION OF OUR NAMED EXECUTIVE OFFICERS <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(&#147;SAY-ON-PAY&#148;)</FONT></FONT> </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We are seeking an advisory vote from our stockholders to approve the compensation paid to the Named Executive Officers, as disclosed in this proxy
statement pursuant to the compensation disclosure rules of the SEC. Unless you indicate otherwise, your proxy will vote <B>FOR</B> the approval of the compensation paid to the Named Executive Officers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee, with assistance from its independent executive compensation consultant and counsel, has structured our executive compensation
program to reflect our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#147;pay-for-performance&#148;</FONT></FONT> philosophy. A significant portion of the compensation opportunities provided to the Named Executive Officers are
dependent on our financial performance, which are intended to drive the creation of stockholder value. The Compensation Committee intends to continue to emphasize responsible compensation arrangements that attract, retain and motivate high caliber
executive officers, motivate these executive officers to achieve our short-term and long-term business strategies and objectives and support our career development and succession goals. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We have determined to hold a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#147;say-on-pay&#148;</FONT></FONT> advisory vote every
year. In accordance with this determination and Section&nbsp;14A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and as a matter of good corporate governance, you have the opportunity to vote &#147;for&#148; or &#147;against,&#148; or to
&#147;abstain&#148; from voting on, the following <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-binding</FONT> resolution relating to executive compensation: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:9%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">&#147;Resolved, that the stockholders approve, on an advisory basis, the compensation paid to the Company&#146;s named executive officers as disclosed in
the Company&#146;s proxy statement for the 2021 annual meeting of stockholders pursuant to the compensation disclosure rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission, including the compensation discussion and analysis, the compensation tables and
the narrative discussion of such proxy statement.&#148; </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In deciding how to vote on this proposal, you are encouraged to consider our executive
compensation philosophy and objectives and the elements of our executive compensation program, as contained in the &#147;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#148; above, as well as the following principles of our executive compensation program and
other information: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

The Compensation Committee places a strong emphasis on performance-based compensation. To this end, approximately 94% of Dr.&nbsp;Su&#146;s and 86% of the other Named Executive Officer&#146;s aggregate total direct compensation opportunity (i.e.,
base salary, annual target cash performance bonus opportunity and target value of annual long-term equity awards for 2020) was in the form of a cash performance bonus and long-term equity awards. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

Committee has implemented &#147;claw-back&#148; provisions and policies applicable to equity awards granted since May 2010 to employees at or above the senior vice president level, which includes all of the Named Executive Officers.
</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt"><U>Pay Practices Aligned with Sound Risk Management</U>. The Compensation Committee endeavors to structure our executive
compensation program to motivate and reward the Named Executive Officers for appropriately balancing opportunity and risk, such as investing in key initiatives designed to advance our growth in existing and new markets while at the same time
avoiding pay practices that encourage excessive risk-taking. In connection with the Compensation Committee&#146;s review of our compensation policies and practices for all employees in general, the Compensation Committee concluded that these
policies and practices do not create risks that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on us. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
